resources.string: Whole-lung ventilation at fixed inputs. Dead space is the part of each breath not exchanging gas. This does not calculate blood oxygen, carbon dioxide or a ventilator setting.

Whole-nephron mass balance for an unspecified, freely filtered solute. Reabsorption is a fraction of the filtered load; secretion is a separate net addition. It is not urine volume, GFR, a drug dose or the isolated function of one tubular cell.

An ideal membrane permeable only to potassium at 37 °C, using concentrations as activities. This is not a real neuron’s resting potential or an action-potential simulation; other ions, pumps and permeability changes are excluded.
Alveolar ventilation = respiratory rate × (tidal volume − dead space) ÷ 1,000.
Excretion = filtered load − reabsorbed amount + secreted amount.
Eₖ = (RT/F) × ln(K outside / K inside); T = 310.15 K, charge = +1. Result shown in mV.
